6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A name made only of replaced or trailing characters gives a folder name ending in a space**\n\n`validateWorkspaceName` accepts a name like `?`, `...` or `-`. In `newWorkspaceFolderName`, `?` turns into `-`, and the trailing-strip regex then removes it, so `safe` ends up as `\"\"`. The function then returns `\"Kaipu Record — \"`, which ends in a space: the same trailing space the doc comment says Windows refuses. On macOS a second name like that (for example `*`) collides with the first folder, and `create` refuses it as `exists`. A possible fix: when `safe` is empty, fall back to a placeholder, or strip the trailing space from the whole result. Another option is to reject such names in validation.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
7	    "replies": [
8	      {
9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0. Runs of unsafe characters now become one dash and only dots and spaces are stripped from the end, so `?` gives `Kaipu Record — -`. A name that leaves nothing (`...`) falls back to `workspace`. Tests in `workspace-name.test.ts` check the folder name never ends in a space. `?` and `*` still map to the same folder; `create` then refuses the second as \"exists\" and the dialog says so, which I think is the right outcome."
11	      }

18	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit rollback leaves a newly written identity.json when the folder had none before**\n\nWhen the registry write fails, the rollback only restores the folder's file if `previous.kind === \"ok\"`. Take a pending entry whose folder is reachable but has no `identity.json` (`previous` is missing). `edit` writes a fresh identity at line 581 with the entry's id and the new name. If `update` then throws, that file stays on disk. The next probe finds an identity with the matching id and adopts it, so the change that was refused shows up again. Calling `removeIdentity(entry.path)` in the non-ok case would undo it the way `create`'s `undo` does.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

21	        "author": "csdev19",
22	        "body": "Fixed in 886d67f0: the rollback also calls `removeIdentity` when the folder had no file. In practice the probe at the start of `edit` rewrites a missing identity first, so `previous` is normally `ok` by then; I added a test for that real path (the old file is back after a failed registry write) and kept the `absent` branch as the guard for the race."

If the payload is malformed only in its color, it should report `invalid-color`, which `WorkspaceCreateRefusal` already has. Otherwise the renderer would flag the name field. Splitting the check into two would report the right field.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

So two concurrent edits, or an edit racing a create, can both pass the check and leave two workspaces with the same name. When an edit is refused with `not-writable` (main returns this when the identity write fails; see `registry-create-edit.test.ts:384`), the dialog shows `createNotWritable`: \"Kaipu couldn't write there, so nothing was created.\" (`packages/i18n/messages/en.json:2605`). If the `alive` guard in `workspace-dialog.tsx:83` were removed, the late `.then` would call `setLocation` outside `act`. React schedules that render through its scheduler, not inside the same microtask, so `queryByText(...Wo)` would still return null and the test would pass anyway. To make the test catch the bug, wait for any pending render before the assertion, for example `await act(async () => answerFirst(...))`, or assert inside a `waitFor` that runs after a macrotask, and keep checking that the \"Work\" path is still shown.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

90	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… refuses the moved folder of a `pendingInit` workspace, which is the case it is meant to fix (confidence medium)**\n\n`open()` registers the migrated Default workspace with `pendingInit` when the old `vaultDirectory` is unplugged at upgrade (lines 298-303). In that case no `identity.json` was ever written to that folder. Suppose the drive comes back at a different mount path. That is the case the not-connected notice's button exists for. The folder has `.kaipu/` sidecars and no identity, so `checkRelocate` reaches line 809 and returns `has-items-no-identity`. The user is told the folder \"isn't one of your workspaces\" and cannot repoint it.\n\nThe same rule hits a `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder already holds an identity with another id. Line 802 refuses it as `different`, but `availability` adopts that id at lines 678-687.\n\nA possible fix: when `entry.pendingInit` is set, accept a folder with no identity (the probe writes it later). For a folder with another workspace's identity, apply the same `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` adoption rule that `availability` uses.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

97	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Relocating the active workspace throws away a pending quiet capture that could still be saved (confidence medium)**\n\n`relocateActive` calls `dropPendingCaptures()`, which dismisses the capture toast and clears the retained PNG (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts:975-978`). That makes sense for a switch, where the capture belongs to the old workspace. After a relocate the workspace id stays the same, and the toast's save goes through `saveCaptureToWorkspace(workspaceId, …)` → `workspaceGate().runActive(workspaceId, …)` (`screenshot-save.ts:87-95`). That save would still succeed and land in the new folder. As written, an unsaved screenshot disappears without explanation when the user picks the workspace's new folder. Consider leaving `dropPendingCaptures` out of the relocate transaction.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

104	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Picking the active workspace's current folder still runs the full transaction (confidence high)**\n\n`checkRelocate` returns `{ ok: true }` when the picked folder is the one already registered: identity id matches (line 802), or same path (line 808). For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` still calls `relocateActive`. That asks every window to prepare (an unsaved editor gets the Save/Discard/Cancel question), bumps the generation (routes remount) and drops pending captures, all for a no-op. Picking the same folder is easy to do, because the picker opens at `dirname(entry.path)` (`index.ts:331`). This PR's own backlog doc also says Move to is part 2 and \"still to build\" (`apps/documentation/src/content/docs/backlog/several-workspaces.md:27`). A user who picks a plain folder is told to use an action they can't find. The Spanish text has the same problem (`es.json:2621`, «Mover a»).\n\nFix: drop the last sentence from both locales until part 2 ships, and drop the `“Move to”` assertion at `workspace-dialog.test.tsx:279`.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

For example, `relocateActive` rethrows when `apply()` throws (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/switch-transaction.ts:121-124`), and `dialog.showOpenDialog`, `reg.availability` and `broadcastState` (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:334-345`) aren't wrapped either. When that happens, the dialog's `changeFolder` only re-enables the button in `finally`, without setting `folderError`. The context's `changeFolder` (`workspaces-context.tsx:174`) shows no toast. Both are called with `void`, so the rejection goes unhandled and the user gets no response to the click. `submit` and `remove` follow the same pattern, so this matches the existing code. A `catch` that shows `relocateFailed` (the key already exists) would make the failure visible.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

It never changes the folder or the name and color, so it would still pass if a relocate enabled Save, or if a name change no longer did. To match the name: resolve a relocate (`onRelocated` called), check that Save is still disabled, then change the color and check that Save becomes enabled. contracts.action: Deferred color upgrade written on reconnect only if the folder still holds the old Default and rose
contracts.before_after: Before: upgrade reused pendingIdentity and overwrote the folder's file. After: it re-reads the identity and writes only when isOldDefault, otherwise the folder's file wins and the marker is dropped (lines 691-707). An edit clears the marker (line 629).
contracts.visible_effect: A Default changed on another Mac while this folder was away is no longer overwritten.
contracts.failure_mode: A write failure is swallowed and the marker stays, so the next probe retries.

contracts.action: Picking the workspace's current folder in Change folder returns early
contracts.before_after: Before: the active workspace always ran the full transaction. After: same-path picks return before it, so no window is asked to save and no route remounts.
contracts.visible_effect: No remount or save prompt on a no-op pick.
contracts.failure_mode: checkRelocate runs first, so a refusal still surfaces.

contracts.action: Rejected create, edit and relocate IPC calls show an 'uncertain' message
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection was unhandled and silent. After: the dialog shows an alert or toast, and the finally block still frees the busy flag.
contracts.visible_effect: Visible message that tells the user to check before retrying.

thread_replies.reply: checkRelocate now accepts a folder that has Kaipu items and no identity when the entry is pendingInit (registry.ts:848), and the new test covers it. The other case you raised, a moved folder holding a different workspace's identity for a pendingInit entry, is still refused as `different`. That is a narrower edge and I'm not blocking on it.
relocateActive still drops pending captures after a relocate, and this round did not touch it. Please decide whether the toast's save should survive a relocate, since the workspace id stays the same.
relocate.ts:39-43 now returns early with the unchanged entry when the picked folder is the current one, and a test checks that no window is asked to save and the generation does not change.
The 'Move to' sentence is gone from en.json and es.json, and the test now asserts its absence.

Both the dialog and the context's changeFolder now catch a rejection and show relocateUncertain. I used 'uncertain' wording instead of relocateFailed, which fits a rejection after main may already have applied the change.
The test now resolves a relocate first, checks that Save is still disabled, then changes the color and checks that Save becomes enabled.

Of the open threads, only the one about relocating the active workspace dropping pending captures is still open. I did not check the `different`-identity pendingInit relocate case beyond the registry code I read.
